Implemented discrete scale training in scale/mod.ts: string-valued columns auto-detected as factors (isDiscreteAes), sorted-unique or explicit-domain level ordering (discreteLevels), and a scalePosition() helper mapping raw values to level-index positions. Wired through compile/mod.ts (numericRange for view domains, positionsOf/lowerLayer now use resolved per-layer mapping + trained scales). Added scaleXDiscrete/scaleYDiscrete DSL builders and two pipeline tests covering auto-sorted levels and explicit domain ordering.

Implemented statCount in stat/mod.ts: tallies rows per distinct x value (preserving original value type via a firstSeen map, first-appearance ordering), outputs a count column, and maps y to count unless the layer already declares a y mapping. Registered in the stat REGISTRY, exported scalePosition from mod.ts, and added two unit tests against applyStat directly.

Wired into compile/mod.ts: mapped color/fill columns now produce a per-point colors array on Point/Line nodes instead of a single flat color. Added scaleFill DSL builder alongside scaleColor. 4 new tests covering discrete assignment, continuous gradient interpolation, and explicit domain/range overrides.

Implemented statBin in stat/mod.ts: bins continuous x into fixed-width ranges (explicit params.binwidth, or params.bins defaulting to ggplot2's 30), producing count and density columns keyed by bin center, with y mapped to count unless the layer already declares y. Implemented geom_area/geom_ribbon lowering to a Polygon RenderNode. Added 'ribbon' to GeomKind (ir/types.ts) and a geomRibbon DSL builder alongside the existing geomArea. compile/mod.ts gained bandPositions(): builds a closed polygon loop (top edge ymax x-ascending, bottom edge ymin x-descending, geom_area defaulting ymin to a 0 baseline when unmapped) and lowers to <Polygon positions fill>. Also extended scale/mod.ts's y-domain training to fold in ymin/ymax columns (previously only mapping.y was considered), so a ribbon/area's trained view range actually spans its band instead of clipping it. 3 new tests covering area's 0-baseline band, ribbon's ymin/ymax band, and the widened y-domain training.

Implemented log10/sqrt transforms, confirmed+tested user domain limits, and opt-in axis expansion. scale/mod.ts: added transformFor() (log10/sqrt/identity) applied both to scalePosition's per-value mapping and to the trained continuous domain (so declared limits are transformed consistently with plotted points), and expandRange() ([mult,add] padding, ggplot2's expansion()) applied only when a scale explicitly sets 'expand' -- kept off by default to avoid silently changing every existing chart's trained range. Wired expand support into compile.ts's discrete numericRange() too. Added scaleXLog10/scaleYLog10/scaleXSqrt/scaleYSqrt DSL builders (ir/types.ts Scale gained an 'expand' field). Scope note: real ggplot2 enables ~5% continuous / 0.6-unit discrete expansion by default; I deliberately kept it off-by-default here since flipping every chart's default range would require rewriting the numeric expectations of most existing exact-match tests without a chance for review -- left as a clearly-documented, fully working opt-in mechanism instead. 4 new tests covering log/sqrt transform+domain, explicit domain limits, and expand padding; all 18 tests pass.

Implemented size/alpha/shape scale training and wired size into rendering. scale/mod.ts: trainContinuousAuxScale (shared by size/alpha, default ranges [1,6] and [0.1,1]) and trainShapeScale (discrete factor levels -> a fixed 6-glyph palette, same fixed-order pattern as the categorical color palette), plus scaleSizeValue/scaleAlphaValue (linear interpolation into range) and scaleShapeValue (level lookup) value functions. Wired size into compile.ts: a mapped size column now produces a per-point 'sizes' array on the Point node (UseGPU's Point supports per-vertex sizes). Also added a flat layer.params.alpha -> 'opacity' passthrough for point/line, since UseGPU's Point/Line only expose a single scalar opacity (no per-vertex opacities array) -- so aesthetic-mapped alpha and shape are trained/testable at the scale layer (scaleAlphaValue/scaleShapeValue) but not wired into per-point rendering, since the underlying renderer has no per-vertex prop for either; documented this as a real, current renderer constraint rather than a gap in this ticket's implementation. Added scaleSize/scaleAlpha/scaleShape DSL builders. 4 new tests covering mapped size on Point, the two interpolation value functions, shape level lookup, and the flat alpha->opacity passthrough; all 22 tests pass.

Implemented the two missing pieces of aesthetic inheritance/override semantics (layer mapping/data overriding plot defaults, and fixed vs mapped aes were already correctly handled by the existing Aes vs Layer.params split). 1) inherit.aes=FALSE equivalent: Layer gained an inheritAes?: boolean field (ir/types.ts) and geom() DSL builders accept an inheritAes option; compile.ts's stage-1 mapping resolution now uses only the layer's own mapping (ignoring spec.mapping entirely) when inheritAes===false, instead of always merging plot+layer mapping. 2) group aesthetic: added splitByGroup() in compile.ts, which partitions a layer's rows by its mapped group column (first-seen order) before lowering; geom_line/path/area/ribbon now render one connected Line/Polygon per group instead of zigzagging across all groups' points in raw data order. lowerLayer() was changed to return RenderNode[] (flatMapped in compile()) to support the one-node-per-group case; geom_point is unaffected since group has no connectivity meaning for independent points. 2 new tests covering group-split lines and inheritAes:false; all 24 tests pass.

Implemented position adjustments in a new packages/core/src/position/mod.ts: stackBars (stack rows sharing an x on top of each other in group-key order, or 'identity' for an unstacked shared baseline), the 'fill' mode within stackBars (normalizes each x's stack to [0,1]), dodgeBars (side-by-side placement with a stable per-group slot across all x values, sorted group-key order so a group's slot doesn't shift between x's), and jitter (uniform random nudge within +/-amount). Exported from mod.ts for direct testing. 3 new unit tests plus integration coverage via the geom_bar/col tests in the paired v04.1 close.

Implemented geom_bar/geom_col rendering: lowerBarLayer() in compile.ts builds one Polygon RenderNode per layer, with one 4-point rectangle loop per bar (positions: [number,number][][], one fill color per loop via 'fills' unless every bar shares one color). Bar width = 0.9 * bandwidth (1 level-index unit for discrete x, else the smallest gap between distinct continuous x's), matching ggplot2's default width=0.9. Wired to position/mod.ts's stackBars/dodgeBars per layer.position (geomBar/geomCol now default to position='stack', ggplot2's real default, via a new defaultPosition param on the geom() DSL builder). Also fixed y-domain training: stacked/filled bars need the *summed* per-x height, not any single row's y, so added widenForStackedBars() to extend the trained y range to the max stack total (or exactly [0,1] for 'fill' -- the raw pre-normalization y domain doesn't describe fill-mode's actual rendered positions, which was a bug I caught and fixed while writing the fill test). geom_point also gained position='jitter' support (uniform random x/y nudge, default amount = 0.4 * x-bandwidth / 0.4 y-units, overridable via width/height params). 4 new pipeline tests (stack, dodge, fill, jitter) covering exact bar geometry, fill colors, and widened y-domains; all 31 tests pass.

Implemented geom_tile/geom_raster via the same Polygon-loop pattern as bars (a scoped deviation from the ticket's 'pairs with Surface/tensor source' hint -- @use-gpu/plot's Surface/tensor-source layers are a specialized GPU scalar-field pipeline I haven't verified against a working render given the still-open WASM blocker, whereas N-rectangle Polygon loops are consistent with the already-established, tested Point/Line/Polygon architecture and fully correct for tile-grid rendering). lowerTileLayer() in compile.ts: one rectangle per row, centered on (x,y), sized to each axis's resolution (smallest gap between distinct values, or 1 level-index unit for discrete) by default so adjacent cells tile edge-to-edge with no gaps -- params.width/height override it. Added widenForTileAxis() to extend both x and y domains by half a cell so edge tiles aren't clipped (tiles extend past their center point, unlike point-based marks). geomTile and geomRaster DSL builders (both map to the same 'tile' GeomKind; geom_raster's real distinction -- always full resolution, no custom width/height -- isn't hard-enforced, a minor simplification). 2 new tests: exact grid positions + widened domain, and a no-gap edge-to-edge sanity check; all 33 tests pass.

Implemented geom_boxplot/geom_errorbar as pre-summarized statistical geoms composed of lines + rects (scope note: this covers the geometry/rendering the ticket describes, not a stat_boxplot quantile-computing stat -- StatKind has no 'boxplot' entry yet, so both geoms currently expect pre-computed columns via aes(), same pattern as geom_ribbon's ymin/ymax; computing quantiles from raw y would be a separate stat ticket). Added 'lower'/'middle'/'upper' aesthetics and 'boxplot'/'errorbar' GeomKinds (ir/types.ts), geomBoxplot/geomErrorbar DSL builders. compile.ts: lowerErrorbarLayer emits one Line of disjoint segments (top cap, vertical stem, bottom cap) per row, width defaulting to 0.9x resolution (ggplot2's bar-style default); lowerBoxplotLayer emits a box Polygon (lower..upper) plus a Line of median + both whisker stems + half-width caps, box width defaulting to 0.75x resolution (ggplot2's default). Both reuse the resolutionOf/colorsOf helpers already established for bars/tiles. y-domain training already covered via the existing ymin/ymax handling in scale/mod.ts (lower/middle/upper fall within that range so need no separate widening). 2 new tests with exact hand-verified segment/box geometry; all 35 tests pass.

Implemented geom_text/geom_label via @use-gpu/plot's Label component. Added Label to GGPlot.tsx's render REGISTRY (it was already in ComponentName/rendertree.ts and emit/mod.ts's PLOT_IMPORTS but never wired to the actual component, so it was previously unusable). lowerTextLayer() in compile.ts builds one Label node per layer: per-point positions (reusing positionsOf) + a 'labels' array from the mapped label column (stringified), plus per-point colors when color/fill is mapped. geomLabel added as a DSL alias for geomText -- both currently render identically, since geom_label's background box needs real text-metrics-aware sizing that requires the font pipeline (same blocker as gggplot-6dm.6), documented as a scoped simplification. 1 new test covering exact Label positions/labels plus emitSource output. All 36 tests pass. This closes out the Geoms library epic (gggplot-v04) at 5/5.

Output path defaults to the spec's basename with a .tsx extension; component name defaults to a PascalCase-ified output filename, overridable via --name=. Root-caused and fixed via empirical testing: added a diagnostic probe plugin to vite.config.ts that logged resolveId/load calls for any '.wasm'-related module id -- it never fired once during a full build, proving Rolldown (Vite 8's default bundler, replacing Rollup) handles .wasm imports through its own native asset pipeline that bypasses the JS plugin container entirely, so vite-plugin-wasm's Rollup-style hooks never got a chance to run on @use-gpu/glyph's wasm-bindgen import. Fix: pinned apps/site's vite to ^7.3.0 (last major line with rollup as a real dependency, not rolldown) and @vitejs/plugin-react to ^5.2.0 (the only version supporting vite ^7 as well as ^8). Rebuilt: grep for WebAssembly/instantiate in the bundle now finds real instantiation glue code (previously zero matches), and the wasm file loads with 200 OK in-browser with zero console errors. Verified via Playwright screenshot -- no more 'wasm.userusttext_new' crash.

Completed now that the WASM blocker (gggplot-6dm.6) is fixed, giving me a working browser to actually tune against. Two more real bugs found and fixed via in-browser inspection (as the ticket asked): 1) Cartesian's range prop maps data into a normalized ~[-1,1] local box, but FlatCamera's default (non-relative) orthogonal projection expects raw PIXEL-unit world coordinates -- without a bridge, tiny normalized values got misread as pixel coordinates, collapsing every mark into the canvas corner. Fixed by wrapping compile()'s output in an Embedded(normalize=true) RenderNode (added 'Embedded' to ComponentName/GGPlot.tsx's REGISTRY/emit's PLOT_IMPORTS), which reads FlatCamera's LayoutContext and correctly rescales Cartesian's normalized output to fill the actual canvas. Embedded also establishes the Plot wrapper internally, so it replaces the old explicit root Plot node rather than nesting inside it. 2) apps/site's ChartCanvas.tsx's frame div wasn't a CSS positioning context, so LiveCanvas's canvas element (which UseGPU renders with position:absolute; top:0; left:0) escaped to the document root instead of filling its frame -- confirmed via getBoundingClientRect on all 3 gallery canvases (all reported rect (0,0), stacked on top of each other at the page's absolute top-left). Fixed with a one-line 'position: relative' on the frame style. Verified end-to-end via Playwright: all 3 gallery examples now render correctly and independently -- scatter+line (blue points, red connecting line), discrete-x factor scatter, and the categorical color-mapped scatter, each in its own frame with correct positions/colors. All 40 tests still pass.

Fixed: added sortByX() in compile.ts, which reorders every column by ascending x. Applied only to the 'line' case (per group, since sorting happens after splitByGroup) -- geom_path continues to preserve raw row order for trajectory-style plots where visit order matters. 1 new test with unsorted input data confirms geom_line reorders to [[0,10],[1,20],[2,30]] while geom_path keeps the original [[2,30],[0,10],[1,20]] order. All 41 tests pass.

Implemented and visually verified both. Researched @use-gpu/plot's compiled Cartesian/Polar source before implementing (not guessed): both share the same range/axes trait shape, and 'axes' is a swizzle string applied AFTER the range-to-clip-space matrix is built -- so coord_flip is just axes:'yx' on the panel + Grid (verified: range/positions stay untouched, only the rendered orientation swaps; confirmed visually as clean horizontal bars). coord_polar selects the Polar view component and passes through spec.coord.params (bend/on/helix) -- confirmed via Playwright that point geoms bend correctly into a circular layout. However, visual verification also surfaced a real, deeper limitation: Polygon's straight 2-point edges don't curve under Polar's nonlinear per-vertex shader transform (only endpoints bend, leaving straight chords), so geom_bar/col renders as a distorted fan instead of clean pie wedges, and Grid has the same issue. This mirrors ggplot2's coord_munch() problem exactly (subdividing straight paths before a non-linear coordinate transform) -- filed as gggplot-97e.4 rather than silently shipping broken-looking bar/polygon polar charts. Added FlippedBars and PolarPoints to the doc site gallery, both DSL builders (coordFlip/coordPolar) already existed. 2 new tests covering axes swizzle + params passthrough; all 43 tests pass.

Implemented stat_smooth with method='lm' (ordinary least-squares linear regression) in packages/core/src/stat/mod.ts. Re-emits x as params.n (default 80) evenly spaced points across the data's x range (bin-center style, like stat_bin), with fitted y, and unless params.se===false, ymin/ymax for a CI ribbon -- mapping.y/ymin/ymax always overridden to the new column names since the fitted point count differs from the input row count. CI band uses the standard OLS prediction formula se(y_hat) = s*sqrt(1/n + (x-xbar)^2/Sxx) but a fixed z=1.96 multiplier rather than the exact Student's-t critical value (large-sample approximation, documented in a code comment as a known simplification -- not a full stats package). loess (ggplot2's default method) is NOT implemented -- it's a substantially bigger lift (weighted local regression with a bandwidth/span parameter); an unrecognized method value warns and falls back to lm. Added geomSmooth() to the DSL (packages/core/src/dsl/mod.ts) and a 'smooth' GeomKind (ir/types.ts). Wired rendering in compile/mod.ts: geom_smooth lowers to an optional Ribbon Polygon (drawn first, light-indigo #c7d2fe fill, only when ymin/ymax are mapped) plus a Line for the fit -- reuses the existing bandPositions/positionsOf helpers. y-domain widening for the ribbon comes for free since trainScales already unions mapping.y/ymin/ymax for the y aesthetic. Tested with exact-value assertions: stat_smooth against noise-free linear data (y=2x+1, zero residual -> deterministic fitted values and a zero-width CI band, verifying the regression math exactly), se:false omitting ymin/ymax, and full compile() tests checking the Line+Polygon RenderNode shapes and that se:false skips the Polygon entirely. 4 new tests, all passing.

Implemented stat_summary in packages/core/src/stat/mod.ts: aggregates y per distinct x value (first-seen order) via params.fun, default 'mean', also 'median'/'sum'/'min'/'max' by name, or a custom (values: number[]) => number function. Only x/y are re-emitted (one row per x group) -- like the existing stat_count/stat_bin, other per-row columns (e.g. a fill/group column) don't have a well-defined per-group value and are dropped; this is a pre-existing pattern/limitation in this codebase, not new. No new geom was added: ggplot2 defaults stat_summary to geom_pointrange, which this codebase doesn't implement, so stat_summary is used by overriding an existing geom's stat, e.g. geomPoint({ stat: 'summary', fun: 'median' }) -- consistent with how GeomOpts.stat already lets any geom override its default stat. Tested with exact-value assertions: default mean aggregation, fun:'median', and a custom aggregator function, all via applyStat directly (matching the stat_count/stat_bin test style). 3 new tests, all passing. deno task check and deno task --cwd packages/core test both pass (50 tests total, up from 43).

Implemented theme -> UseGPU props mapping. Theme gained background/grid/gridColor/gridWidth/axisColor/axisWidth/fontFamily/fontSize/textColor fields (ir/types.ts); compile.ts maps these onto Grid/Axis width+color traits and geom_text's Label size/color/family (falling back to theme values only when the layer doesn't set its own param). theme_*() calls now merge additively (dsl/mod.ts's GG.add: {...this.spec.theme, ...part.value}) matching ggplot2's theme_minimal() + theme(...) composition instead of the previous full-replace behavior. Added themeClassic() (grid:false), themeGrey() (grey background + white grid), and a general theme(overrides) builder mirroring ggplot2's theme(...). 5 new headless tests with exact-value assertions (default/themeGrey/themeClassic/merge-behavior/font-fallback), all passing, plus live-in-browser Playwright verification that grid/axis color+width overrides and geom_text font theming render correctly. Known limitation, tracked separately as gggplot-b15.4: theme.background draws an opaque full-panel Polygon first in the guides array (correct in the RenderTree/emitSource output, verified structurally), but in this project's live WebGPU backend it causes the following Grid/Axis draws to render invisibly -- zBias/depthWrite/depthTest toggles on the Polygon didn't fix it, root mechanism still unknown. Scoped out of the live gallery demo (ThemedChart example uses grid/axis/font theming only, with a note pointing to b15.4) rather than shipping a visually broken background.

Implemented facet_wrap/facet_grid: partitions data by facet vars before stat transform (so stat_count/bin aggregate per-panel), trains shared/fixed scales across all panels (ggplot2 default), and lays out panels via a new custom FacetGrid Live component that subdivides the ambient LayoutContext pixel rect at render time (not a real @use-gpu/plot export -- documented in rendertree.ts/GGPlot.tsx; emitSource inlines its definition for standalone output). 5 new exact-value pipeline tests + verified live in-browser via Playwright screenshot: a facet_wrap(cyl) scatter renders 3 correctly-positioned, correctly-scaled panels in a 2x2 grid. Strip labels (facet value as text) compile correctly but don't visually render yet -- confirmed via Playwright this is the same pre-existing FontLoader 'fontless-by-default' gap that already affects geom_text (not a new regression, not in scope here).
